notes: Second sweep at db91c23: five runs (opus-1, haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1, sonnet-2), all rc 0 with the expected model_id. All five read SKILL.md (opus-1 also read references/library-design.md), which meets Expected reads, and each transcript contains the reworded `with` paragraph. In the scratch folder, with Decimal 2.3.0 built from the local Hex cache on the code path, all five pass mix format --check-formatted, compile with --warnings-as-errors and pass their doctests (opus-1 2, haiku-2 1, sonnet-1 1, sonnet-2 2; haiku-1 has none). A probe gives correct totals and dates for a mixed sample and {:error, reason} from all five for a bad amount, an unknown status and a missing key; haiku-1's missing-key error carries the whole row instead of naming the field.

Changed rule, graded against the current text: "Chain fallible steps with `with`; normalize each step's error in a small private function". The one-step verdict is decided by "A `with` has at least two `<-` steps; one step is a `case`." (idiomatic-elixir/SKILL.md line 118) and "When the body of a one-step `with` calls another function that can fail, that call is the second step: chain it with a second `<-` instead of nesting a `case` or adding an `else`." (line 150). Violating runs out of 5: one-step `with` 2 (sonnet-1 line 77, sonnet-2 line 82, each wrapping parse_orders/1 in build/1; the body calls nothing that can fail); a `case` nested in a `with` body 0; `else` 0 (no run writes one). Opus-1, haiku-1 and haiku-2 handle the same single call with case (lines 195, 29, 63), and all five chain their lookups and parses in one multi-step with (opus-1 46-50, haiku-1 53-55, haiku-2 127-134, sonnet-1 98-105, sonnet-2 107-114). Comparison: both 2026-10-21 check batches had 2 of 4, both Sonnet, in the same build/1 spot, and the previous sweep's skill runs had the shape in all four Haiku and Sonnet runs (per the second check batch's re-read); here Haiku and Opus are clean and Sonnet still writes it in both runs.

Changed rule, graded against the current text: "Use the `Enum` or `Map` function made for the job", decided by its second table row: "a `reduce` that reads and writes one key per element is these two written by hand" (idiomatic-elixir/SKILL.md line 217). Hand-written per-key fold: 1 of 5 (haiku-1 lines 109-110, an Enum.reduce with Map.update/4 per currency summing Decimals, the shape the first check batch said the previous sweep's skill-sonnet-2 would count as under this row). The case's check line now names Enum.group_by/2: all five group customers with it (opus-1 224, haiku-1 98, haiku-2 74, sonnet-1 146, sonnet-2 156), and all but haiku-1 also group each customer's completed orders by currency with it (opus-1 240, haiku-2 87, sonnet-1 169, sonnet-2 172). Decimal sums with Enum.reduce and Decimal.add/2 are reductions no table row replaces, as before. Completed orders are counted with Enum.frequencies_by/2 in four runs and with Enum.count/2 per customer group in sonnet-1 (line 178), held clean as the second check batch held haiku-2's Enum.count/1.

Changed rule, graded against the current text: Naming (fetch sentence: "A function that looks a key up and also checks the value, returning `{:error, reason}`, is not a `fetch`: name it by its job, such as `string_field/2` or `parse_amount/1`." line 294; variable sentence: "A variable may carry the name of the external key it holds, as in `%{"data" => data}`, since the payload chose that name." line 297). Violating runs per sentence, out of 5: modules CamelCase and snake_case 0; top-level namespace 0 (Reports.Orders as the prompt names it, other modules nested under it); boolean functions end in ? 0 (opus-1 and haiku-2 define completed?/1, the others define none); get/fetch 0 (opus-1 names its lookup-and-check helper field/3, haiku-2, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 string_field/2, haiku-1 matches the keys in the head; the previous sweep's opus-1, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 skill runs named such a helper fetch_field); size/length 0 (not exercised); ignored values 0; domain variable names 0 (no data, item, res, x or single letters; text, value and parsed held to the earlier standard; the external-key exception was not needed).

Unchanged rule: "Use captures for one-call lambdas and `fn` for anything longer", decided by "When the body does more than one call or would need `&2`, write `fn` with named arguments." (idiomatic-elixir/SKILL.md line 336). `&2` sentence: 1 of 5 (sonnet-1 line 171: &Decimal.add(&1.amount, &2)). The second check batch had 2 of 4 (both Sonnet); this sweep's sonnet-2 groups amounts with Enum.group_by/3 and sums with &Decimal.add/2 instead.

Other unchanged rules follow the earlier standard. No run catches Decimal.parse/1 failures with `_ ->`: all five match {amount, ""}, {_amount, _rest} and :error, the three shapes the skill's own one-step `with` example now lists (idiomatic-elixir/SKILL.md lines 164-166), against 4 of 4 Haiku and Sonnet runs in the previous sweep and 3 of 4 in the second check batch. reduce_while piped into `case` (sonnet-1 line 91, sonnet-2 line 100) is not listed, as in the check batches. Haiku-1's @doc without ## Examples is listed under the Comments rule, as the previous sweep listed skill-haiku-2's. Haiku-1 prepends without reversing (line 41); nothing downstream depends on the order, so it is clean, as the second check batch held haiku-2's.
